keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 552-553: Xiao Ji 'declared himself emperor in spring 552' (infobox: Pretender of the Liang Dynasty, May 16, 552 - August 5, 553) and 'governed the modern Sichuan and Chongqing region' as governor of Yi Province, to which he was appointed in 537; Li Province was 'part of Xiao Ji's domain'. Liang Province (Hanzhong) was governed by his cousin Xiao Xun, so Hanzhong is left out. A rebel state Cliopatria lacks; no area on any page.

region.text: Xiao Ji's domain: he 'governed the modern Sichuan and Chongqing region' as governor of Yi Province; headquarters Chengdu

ledger.note: 552: Xiao Ji declares himself emperor in Yi Province. He 'declared himself emperor in spring 552' (infobox: reign from May 16, 552) and 'governed the modern Sichuan and Chongqing region' as governor of Yi Province. The Emperor Yuan page: he claimed the throne 'around the same time' Hou Jing was defeated.

region.text: Xiao Ji's domain: he 'governed the modern Sichuan and Chongqing region' as governor of Yi Province; headquarters Chengdu

ledger.note: 553: the Western Wei invade Yi Province. Xiao Yi 'requested Western Wei to attack Xiao Ji from the rear'; Yuwen Tai 'sent his nephew Yuchi Jiong with an army to attack Yi Province', and Yuchi 'put it under siege'. The page gives no date for Chengdu's fall; the Emperor Yuan page: 'Meanwhile, Western Wei captured Xiao Ji's domain, and that territory would be permanently lost'.

region.text: Xiao Ji's domain: he 'governed the modern Sichuan and Chongqing region' as governor of Yi Province; headquarters Chengdu

ledger.note: 553: Xiao Ji dies and his claim ends. Infobox death August 5, 553; the lead says he 'was killed in battle' after his advancing forces 'were defeated by Emperor Yuan's'; the Emperor Yuan page has Fan board his ship and put him to death on Xiao Yi's orders. The land is the Western Wei's.

wars.outcome: Xiao Yi has Xiao Ji put to death in August 553; the Western Wei capture Xiao Ji's domain and keep it.

certainty.note: The extent of Xiao Ji's domain is not given on any page opened.

notes: A rebel state Cliopatria lacks, written because it held Sichuan for about fifteen months (May 552 to August 553) and the Cliopatria Liang row hides it. Pages: the Xiao Ji article and the Emperor Yuan of Liang page, plus the thin Western Wei page. Pages differ on the death: 'killed in battle' (Xiao Ji lead) against 'Fan boarded Xiao Ji's ship and put him to death' (Emperor Yuan page); both give 5 August 553 through the infobox. The date of the Western Wei's entry into Chengdu is on no page; the extent of the domain is the researcher's reading (Sichuan and Chongqing, from the Xiao Ji page); Hanzhong (Liang Province) was not his. cliopatria_names empty; wikidata null (not checked).
